notes: HELD-OUT case (R13): never tune prompts by looking at its answers — it exists to catch prompt changes that only fit go-http-cache-review. Seeded defects, authored 2026-09-25.

findings.title: SQL injection via f-string
findings.detail: `f"... WHERE id = '{job_id}'"` — job_id is interpolated into SQL. Use a parameterized query (`?`).

findings.title: Unbounded recursive retry
findings.detail: On any failure `process` calls itself again with no attempt limit: a permanently failing job retries forever (growing sleeps, eventually RecursionError).

findings.title: Missing job → TypeError
findings.detail: `fetchone()` returns None for an unknown id and `row[0]` raises TypeError (outside the try).

findings.title: Mutable default argument
findings.detail: `attempts=[]` is shared across ALL calls: the backoff of one job grows with other jobs' failures, and the list grows forever.

findings.title: Bare except
findings.detail: `except:` also catches KeyboardInterrupt/SystemExit/CancelledError and programming errors (KeyError on the job payload), turning them into silent retries.

findings.title: time.sleep blocks the event loop
findings.detail: Blocking sleep inside `async def` freezes every coroutine; use `await asyncio.sleep`.

findings.title: Blocking HTTP client in async code
findings.detail: `requests.post` is synchronous and blocks the loop; use an async client (httpx.AsyncClient/aiohttp) or run_in_executor.

findings.title: Status code not checked
findings.detail: No `raise_for_status()`: an error response body is stored as a successful result (or `.json()` fails and is retried as if transient).

findings.title: Jobs run sequentially
findings.detail: Awaiting coroutines one by one gives no concurrency; use `asyncio.gather`.

findings.title: ZeroDivisionError on an empty id list
Request target taken from stored payload
findings.detail: The POST goes to `job["url"]` from the database without validation — anyone who can write a job can make the worker call internal addresses (SSRF).

findings.title: Module-level DB connection
findings.detail: The sqlite connection is opened at import time, never closed, and not usable across threads.

findings.title: Global retries counter is write-only
findings.detail: `retries` is mutated through `global` but never read — dead, misleading state.
